question.problem:
$$
{{[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & -1 \\ 6 & 9 & 2 \\ 4 & 5 & 2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ \boxed{} & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{L}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & -1 \\ 0 & -3 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{U}
$$

Consider the LU factorization of the matrix $A$ above. What is the value of the entry ${l}_{21}$ in the matrix $L?$
question.worked_solution:
We want to make $0$ at the position ${a}_{21}$ using Gaussian elimination. To do this, we take the $2$nd row of $A,$ and we add the $1$st row of $A$ multiplied by $-3:$

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & -1 \\ 6 & 9 & 2 \\ 4 & 5 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & -1 \\ 0 & -3 & 5 \\ 4 & 5 & 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The entry ${l}_{21}$ of the matrix $L$ is the factor next to ${R}_{1},$ taken with the opposite sign:

$$
{l}_{21}=-(-3)=3.
$$
